html:
Almaty began in 1854 as Fort Verny, "faithful", a Russian fort at the foot of the Trans-Ili Alatau, the northern range of the Tian Shan. It is now the largest city of Kazakhstan, with over two million people.

Russia built the fort as it pushed south into Zhetysu, the land of the "seven rivers", near the site of an older town of the Silk Road. Cossacks and Russian peasants settled around it. Earthquakes struck hard, in 1887 and in the Kebin earthquake of 1911, which ruined most of the town; the wooden Ascension Cathedral survived.

Renamed Alma-Ata in 1921, it became the capital of the Kazakh Soviet republic in 1929 and grew fast after the Turkestan-Siberia Railway arrived in 1930. In December 1986 protests here, the Jeltoqsan, were an early sign of national anger against Soviet rule. It stayed the capital of independent Kazakhstan until Astana became the capital in 1997.
